h1: The 6 Best Desk Lights for Video Calls, Dual-Purpose Lamps and Ring Lights, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Desk Lights for Video Calls: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 desk lights for video calls from Logitech, LitONES and others, compared on colour accuracy, diffusion and dimming.
summary: The Logitech for Creators Litra Glow is the best desk light for video calls, a purpose-built premium LED with face-friendly diffusion. The Zoom Lighting ring light with CRI 97.8 is the best for colour accuracy, the LitONES edge-lit desk lamp does double duty for tasks and calls, and the RALENO 9 inch panel gives the most even spread.
intro: The usual mistake with video call lighting is to treat it as brightness. A webcam sees a screen-lit face as flat and grey, and the instinct is to crank up the nearest lamp. What improves the picture is a large, soft source placed in front of you, because a big diffused light wraps around your features and a small bare LED creates hard shadows and glare on skin.

This ranking sorts six desk lights by the qualities that give a soft, flattering picture: diffusion, colour accuracy, adjustability and how they sit on a desk. We read the product titles and specification lists supplied and avoid quoting lumens that the listings do not give. Where a lamp is mainly a task light, we say so, since it fills a different role from a dedicated video light.

products.name: Logitech for Creators Litra Glow Premium LED Streaming Light - Graphite
products.verdict: A premium LED streaming light engineered to illuminate faces softly.
products.description:
The Litra Glow is a premium LED video light from Logitech for Creators, with diffusion engineered for face illumination and a quality LED driver design. Expect to spend in the $50 to $100 range.

It wins because it is built for exactly this job. Face-focused diffusion spreads the light across a wide panel so skin looks soft, and a good LED driver design should keep the output steady, which helps avoid visible flicker on camera. As a Logitech accessory, it also sits neatly beside a Logitech webcam. The price is higher than the budget ring lights.

Buy it for regular calls and streams where you want a reliable, polished look. Skip it if you only need a light for the odd call.
products.idealFor: Daily callers and streamers wanting a polished look.
products.skipIf: You take only the odd call.

products.name: Zoom Lighting for Computer, Adjustable Desk Lighting for Video Calls, 30 Light Modes Video Conference Light, Desk Ring Light with Stand, CRI 97.8
products.verdict: A desk ring light with a stated CRI of 97.8, 30 light modes and a stand.
products.description:
This desk ring light has a stated CRI of 97.8, 30 light modes and a stand, built for webcam meetings, live streaming and the home office. Expect to spend in the $25 to $50 range.

It ranks second because CRI is the measure of colour accuracy and a figure near 98 means skin tones should look natural. Thirty modes combine colour temperature and brightness, so you can match a lamp-lit room or a bright window. The ring shape can reflect in glasses, and a ring only fills as well as it is positioned.

Choose it if colour accuracy matters and you want options at a low price. Skip it if you wear glasses and cannot angle the light.
products.idealFor: Callers who want natural skin tones.

products.name: LitONES LED Desk Lamp for Home Office, Soft Edge-lit Design - Modern Style
products.verdict: A soft edge-lit LED desk lamp that serves as task light and video call fill light.
products.description:
The LitONES is an LED desk lamp with a soft edge-lit design, positioned as a dual-purpose light for tasks and for video call fill. Expect to spend in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks third because it solves the desk-space problem: one lamp instead of two. An edge-lit panel gives soft, even light without a visible hotspot, and a modern style fits a tidy desk. The trade is that a desk lamp is not tuned for faces the way a video light is, and the listing says nothing about CRI or colour range.

Pick it if you want a single lamp for work and calls. Skip it if you need studio-grade face lighting.
pros: One lamp for tasks and calls
products.idealFor: Small desks that need one multi-use lamp.

products.name: RALENO 9" LED Video Light, 2500K-6500K Camera Light with Desk Stand
products.verdict: A 9 inch LED panel with 2500K to 6500K colour range and a desk stand.
products.description:
The RALENO is a 9 inch LED video light with a 2500K to 6500K colour temperature range and a desk stand. Expect to spend in the $25 to $50 range.

It ranks fourth because a 9 inch panel has a larger diffusion surface than compact ring lights, which gives more even, softer light. The wide colour range lets you move from warm lamp tones at 2500K to cool daylight at 6500K, matching nearly any room. It does not list a CRI.

Choose it for even, adjustable light at a low price. Skip it if you need a stated CRI.
products.idealFor: Soft, even light in changing rooms.

products.name: Desk Ring Light with Stand for Computer, Desk Light for Video Recording
products.verdict: A budget desk ring light with a stand and adjustable colour temperature.
products.description:
This is a desk ring light with a stand and adjustable colour temperature for video recording. Expect to spend in the $25 to $50 range.

It ranks fifth because it covers the basics at a low price without the CRI and mode count of the Zoom Lighting model. Adjustable colour temperature is the key feature, since it lets you match the room. The listing is light on size and brightness.

Buy it for a simple, low-cost light. Skip it if you want stated colour accuracy.

products.name: Airlonv LED Desk Lamp with Clamp, 17" Stepless Dimming Light, Black
products.verdict: A 17 inch clamp-on LED desk lamp with stepless dimming, mainly a task light.
products.description:
The Airlonv is a 17 inch clamp-mounted LED desk lamp with stepless dimming and a general-purpose beam angle. Spend here stays under $25.

The last-place ranking reflects that this is a task lamp with some video call value, not a purpose-built video light. Stepless dimming lets you set exactly the level you need, and the clamp frees desk space. Its beam is general-purpose, so it lights the desk well but does not diffuse for faces.

Buy it as a cheap desk lamp that helps on calls. Skip it as your only video light.
products.idealFor: Desk lighting with some call benefit.
products.skipIf: It must be your video light.

whatMatters.detail: A larger, softer source gives flattering light, while a small bare LED gives harsh shadows. Look for panel size or diffusion on the listing.
CRI measures colour accuracy on a 100-point scale. A stated 97.8 suggests skin tones look natural. Many lights do not state CRI, so a figure is a good sign.
Warm light is yellow and cool light is blue-white. A range such as 2500K to 6500K lets you match your room. Match your window light for the cleanest look.
Place the light slightly above and to the side of the camera, not directly behind it. This lights your face and reduces glasses reflections.
Cheap LEDs can flicker on camera. A quality driver reduces this. Look for words like flicker-free or quality driver.

faq.q: Will a desk lamp be enough for video calls?
faq.a: Sometimes. A diffused lamp placed in front of you can work well, but a dedicated video light gives softer and more adjustable results.
Putting the light behind the monitor or behind you. A backlit face looks dark, so face the light source towards you.

faq.q: Is the Logitech Litra Glow worth it over a ring light?
faq.a: If you call every day, yes. Its diffusion and drivers are better. For occasional calls a ring light is fine.
Easy. Put the light on its stand, plug it into USB or the wall, and adjust the angle and brightness.

faq.q: How do I look after the light?
faq.a: Wipe the diffuser with a soft cloth, keep the cable untangled and avoid blocking the vents on powered models.

faq.q: Do these lights flicker on camera?
faq.a: Quality drivers keep flicker low. Cheaper lights may flicker at low brightness, so use higher settings if you see banding.

finalTake: The Logitech for Creators Litra Glow is the best desk light for video calls, with face-friendly diffusion and a quality driver. The Zoom Lighting ring light with CRI 97.8 is the colour-accurate budget choice, the LitONES lamp does double duty on small desks, and the RALENO 9 inch panel gives the most even light. Place your light above and slightly to one side of the camera.
